messages:
maya: Heads-up — we need to align on how request IDs and spans flow into the Console dashboards. Product wants per-request latency and error bubbles grouped by request_id for the new routing policy UI. Can we sketch what runtime + infra changes are needed?
ryan: Quick q: do we want to force-sample some requests so dashboards can always link traces? Sampling has cost and storage implications.
lee: Runtime-wise we can emit a top-level span tag `redwood.request_id` and set `x-redwood-request-id` on downstream calls. That lets the trace backend group spans by request id. Overhead is minimal if we only tag root spans.
sophia: UX note: Console will need a toggle to enable "request-id linking" (off by default) and a canary rollout per org. Need a fallback when request_id absent.
maya: Proposal: 1) standardize header name `x-redwood-request-id` (UUID v4), 2) runtime adds root span tag `redwood.request_id`, 3) infra sampling rule to always retain 1% of traces and force-keep traces that have `redwood.request_id` flagged for dashboards.
ryan: 1% baseline seems OK but what's the cost spike when we enable request-id linking org-wide? Also what about high-QPS routes + quotas?
lee: If we mark traces with a boolean field `ui_link=true` in the tracespan attr we can instruct the collector to upsample those to retention tier. Implementation: runtime sets `ui_link` when request header present and org opt-in. Collector rules:
```
if span.attributes['ui_link'] == true:
  keep_trace()
elif sample_rate < threshold:
  probabilistic_sample()
```
This avoids huge retention for everything.
sophia: For rollout UX: Console sets org flag; when toggled we send a config to runtime via config service enabling `propagate_request_id=true` and to collector to apply `ui_link` enrichment. Start with a small percent of orgs as canary.
infra-bot: Current sampling rules: global prob_sample=0.01, max_retained_per_min=500. Adding attribute-based keep rule is supported but needs a schema migration in observability. Filed infra ticket #OBS-412.
ryan: Edge case: some downstream vendors (payment, legal) strip unknown headers. How do we ensure request_id survives?
lee: We should add `x-redwood-request-id` to correlation docs and include middleware for common integrations to re-insert from span context. Also add fallback to generate a synthetic request id at the first proxy hop and annotate that in the trace.
maya: Logging: sync logs and traces by request id — runtime should also write `request_id` to the structured logs. Example log line: `{"ts":"...","level":"info","msg":"handle_request","request_id":"b7f3...","route":"/api/v1/generate"}`.
sophia: Dashboard queries: we'll add a derived metric `p90_by_request_id` that aggregates per-request latencies; to keep query cost down we'll only compute for traces retained via `ui_link`.
ryan: SLA/quotas: need to cap the number of `ui_link` traces per org per minute to avoid noisy orgs blowing retention. Maybe default 5/min/org and allow overrides for enterprise.
lee: Agree. Collector should drop `ui_link` beyond cap and emit `ui_link_dropped` metric tagged by org.
maya: Action items: @lee implement root span tag + header propagation middleware (PR in eng-runtime), @ryan estimate cost delta & quota caps, @sophia wire up Console toggle and canary UI, infra team to merge OBS-412 and add retention cap. I'll schedule a follow-up sync Friday. :calendar: 
deploy-bot: [canary] telemetry-config v1.3 deployed to us-west-canary at 1718200075
infra-bot: OBS-412 created: schema migration + attribute-keep-rule. Assigned to @lee.
maya: Thanks — keeping this thread as the tracker. If anyone spots a compliance/regulatory concern about preserving IDs across boundaries call it out now.
